goal.objective:
`src/cli.js` is the program; how the work is split across other files under `src/` is up to you. It takes exactly one argument, `replay` or `summary`, and reads a limiter file from standard input. Split the input on newlines and drop the empty tail a trailing newline leaves. Trim each line; ignore it when it is empty or begins with `#`; otherwise split it on runs of whitespace. Exit 0 whenever the file parses.

A name, a route prefix and an event key are each one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_`, `.`, `/`, `:` and `-`. Every count is an unsigned decimal integer written without a sign and without a leading zero unless it is exactly `0`.

`bucket <name> <capacity> <refill> <per>` declares a token bucket, with a capacity of at least 1, a refill of at least 0, and a period of at least 1. `window <name> <limit> <span>` declares a sliding window, with a limit of at least 0 and a span of at least 1. Two policies may not share a name. `route <prefix> <policy>...` sends every key that starts with that prefix to those policies, in the order written; every policy must already be declared, and two routes may not share a prefix. `event <tick> <key>` is one arrival at that tick, and ticks never go backwards across the file. Once the first event appears no further `bucket`, `window` or `route` line may follow.

Each policy keeps one independent state per key. A key is limited by the route whose prefix it starts with and which is longest among those that match; a key no route matches is always allowed. When an event arrives, every policy on its route first advances to the event's tick, then every one of them is asked, and only when all of them allow it does each of them record it. A denied event changes no policy's stored allowance.

A token bucket holds `capacity` tokens and starts full when a key first reaches it. Advancing it to a tick adds `refill` tokens for every `per` ticks that passed since it last advanced for that key, without ever passing the capacity, and partial periods accumulate exactly: after `n` ticks the bucket holds `refill` times `n` divided by `per` more tokens than it did, and that fraction is never rounded away. It allows a request when it holds at least one whole token, and recording one spends exactly one.

A sliding window remembers the ticks of the requests it recorded for a key. Advancing it to a tick forgets every remembered tick at or before the tick minus the span, so the window covers the `span` ticks ending at the current one. It allows a request when fewer than `limit` ticks remain remembered, and recording one remembers this tick.

`replay` prints one line per event in log order: `<tick> <key> allow`, or `<tick> <key> deny <policy>` naming the first policy on the route, in the order the route wrote them, that refused. `summary` instead prints `<key> allowed=<a> denied=<d>` for every key that saw an event, in ascending key order, and then `total allowed=<a> denied=<d>`.

A failure writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; stop at the first one. The messages are `error: usage: cli.js replay|summary` when the argument is not exactly one of the two mode words, and otherwise `error: line N: <reason>` where the reason is one of `unknown directive <word>`, `expected bucket <name> <capacity> <refill> <per>`, `expected window <name> <limit> <span>`, `expected route <prefix> <policy>...`, `expected event <tick> <key>`, `invalid policy name <name>`, `invalid route prefix <prefix>`, `invalid key <key>`, `policy <name> is declared twice`, `prefix <prefix> is routed twice`, `unknown policy <name>`, `declarations must come before the first event`, `tick T is before tick P`, and `<field> must be an integer of at least <least>` naming the field as `capacity`, `refill`, `per`, `limit`, `span` or `tick`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root. This task is also judged on inputs you do not see: a validator runs your program on its own held-back cases and compares the exit code and output byte for byte. The visible tests cover the main paths only. Implement the written specification, including every corner it states, rather than the behaviour the visible tests happen to pin down.

header.system:
You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

chunk.text:
All 17 tests pass, no `node_modules`, `package.json`/`test/` untouched, and this isn't a git repo (no commit needed).

## Summary

I implemented the rate-limiter simulator across several files under `src/`:

- **`src/tokens.js`** — regex helpers for the shared name/prefix/key charset and for strict unsigned-decimal-integer parsing (no sign, no superfluous leading zero), returning `BigInt`.
- **`src/errors.js`** — `CliError`/`LineError` classes so the CLI can distinguish expected user-facing failures from bugs.
- **`src/policy.js`** — `TokenBucket` and `SlidingWindow` classes, each keeping independent per-key state:
  - `TokenBucket` stores tokens as an exact numerator over `per` (avoiding any rounding of partial refills), starts full on first use, caps at `capacity * per`, and allows/spends whole tokens.
  - `SlidingWindow` stores remembered tick lists per key, trimming ticks `<= tick - span` on advance.
- **`src/parse.js`** — the grammar/validation layer: splits/trims lines, drops the trailing empty line, skips blanks/comments, dispatches on the directive word, checks arity before checking field validity, enforces "declarations before first event," name/prefix/key format, integer field bounds, duplicate policy/prefix detection, unknown-policy references, and global tick monotonicity — throwing `LineError` with the exact required message on the first problem.
- **`src/simulate.js`** — resolves each event's key to the longest matching route prefix (or no route), advances only that route's policies to the event tick, checks all of them, and records on all of them only if every one allows, tracking which policy (in route order) was the first to deny.
- **`src/cli.js`** — validates the single `replay`/`summary` argument, reads all of stdin synchronously (works with piped/non-TTY input), buffers output and only writes to stdout on success, and formats `replay` (per-event lines) or `summary` (per-key + total counts using `BigInt` counters, sorted by key).

Verified beyond the visible suite: usage errors, malformed/negative/leading-zero integers, invalid name/key characters, exact fractional token accumulation (e.g., refill 2 per 3 ticks accumulating precisely across two ticks to reach exactly 1 token), duplicate route prefixes, forward references to undeclared policies, multi-policy deny-ordering, and confirmed no `node_modules` and that `test/`/`package.json` are untouched.

goal.objective:
`src/cli.js` is the program; how the work is split across other files under `src/` is up to you. It takes exactly one argument, `replay` or `summary`, and reads a limiter file from standard input. Split the input on newlines and drop the empty tail a trailing newline leaves. Trim each line; ignore it when it is empty or begins with `#`; otherwise split it on runs of whitespace. Exit 0 whenever the file parses.

A name, a route prefix and an event key are each one or more of the characters `A` to `Z`, `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `_`, `.`, `/`, `:` and `-`. Every count is an unsigned decimal integer written without a sign and without a leading zero unless it is exactly `0`.

`bucket <name> <capacity> <refill> <per>` declares a token bucket, with a capacity of at least 1, a refill of at least 0, and a period of at least 1. `window <name> <limit> <span>` declares a sliding window, with a limit of at least 0 and a span of at least 1. Two policies may not share a name. `route <prefix> <policy>...` sends every key that starts with that prefix to those policies, in the order written; every policy must already be declared, and two routes may not share a prefix. `event <tick> <key>` is one arrival at that tick, and ticks never go backwards across the file. Once the first event appears no further `bucket`, `window` or `route` line may follow.

Each policy keeps one independent state per key. A key is limited by the route whose prefix it starts with and which is longest among those that match; a key no route matches is always allowed. When an event arrives, every policy on its route first advances to the event's tick, then every one of them is asked, and only when all of them allow it does each of them record it. A denied event changes no policy's stored allowance.

A token bucket holds `capacity` tokens and starts full when a key first reaches it. Advancing it to a tick adds `refill` tokens for every `per` ticks that passed since it last advanced for that key, without ever passing the capacity, and partial periods accumulate exactly: after `n` ticks the bucket holds `refill` times `n` divided by `per` more tokens than it did, and that fraction is never rounded away. It allows a request when it holds at least one whole token, and recording one spends exactly one.

A sliding window remembers the ticks of the requests it recorded for a key. Advancing it to a tick forgets every remembered tick at or before the tick minus the span, so the window covers the `span` ticks ending at the current one. It allows a request when fewer than `limit` ticks remain remembered, and recording one remembers this tick.

`replay` prints one line per event in log order: `<tick> <key> allow`, or `<tick> <key> deny <policy>` naming the first policy on the route, in the order the route wrote them, that refused. `summary` instead prints `<key> allowed=<a> denied=<d>` for every key that saw an event, in ascending key order, and then `total allowed=<a> denied=<d>`.

A failure writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; stop at the first one. The messages are `error: usage: cli.js replay|summary` when the argument is not exactly one of the two mode words, and otherwise `error: line N: <reason>` where the reason is one of `unknown directive <word>`, `expected bucket <name> <capacity> <refill> <per>`, `expected window <name> <limit> <span>`, `expected route <prefix> <policy>...`, `expected event <tick> <key>`, `invalid policy name <name>`, `invalid route prefix <prefix>`, `invalid key <key>`, `policy <name> is declared twice`, `prefix <prefix> is routed twice`, `unknown policy <name>`, `declarations must come before the first event`, `tick T is before tick P`, and `<field> must be an integer of at least <least>` naming the field as `capacity`, `refill`, `per`, `limit`, `span` or `tick`.
